decision: Do not add a persistent ThreadPoolExecutor to the GGUF model loop. The measured staged gfx1151 Qwen3.8 server path constructs no generation-side pools. The three per-cycle pool sites belong to direct compatibility/control loops, and an out-of-tree reusable-pool diagnostic did not produce a consistent complete-wall win.

source_inventory.direct_loop_status: compatibility/control/oracle path tracked by docs/REFACTOR.md under GGUF duplicate AR loop ownership

direct_qwen38_dense_c8_control.reason: the dense direct MTP control does not use the three MoE/stream-chunk pool sites

live_qwen36_moe_c8_limitation.error: MoE MTP2 prefill lost its target-hidden sink
live_qwen36_moe_c8_limitation.interpretation: not caused by the 2026-09-05 packed-prefill final-output mask; outside this Qwen3.8 application campaign

host_executor_microbenchmark.protocol: Five trials of 200 cycles per worker count. Each cycle submits one no-op per worker and waits for all results. The control constructs and closes a pool every cycle; the candidate reuses one warmed pool.

legacy_moe_persistent_pool_ab.scope: out-of-tree diagnostic only; one prompt; direct compatibility/control path; not a product or throughput claim
legacy_moe_persistent_pool_ab.interpretation: The draft sub-window consistently improves, which indicates real HIP thread-local startup cost beyond Python pool construction. Complete call and cycle walls win only two of four counterbalanced pairs, however, and this direct loop is not the staged product owner. The result does not satisfy the complete-server/load retention gate.
